Just wrapped our earnings call. It was a very strong close to what was a record fiscal year for Microsoft. · Annual revenue: $331B, +18% · MS Cloud: $214B, + 27% · And Azure: $100B+, +41% And even bigger opportunity ahead! I wanted to share some more perspective on two areas of focus for us: First, we are building a new model system, where the harness, context, memory, and action space are separate from any one model family, thereby moving the frontier on the cost -to-outcome curve. And it’s not just about cost. It also has the added benefit of business continuity and resilience because every model is substitutable. This is the system we are using in our products, with great results. And we are making it available for our customers via Foundry too. You can read more about this from **Mustafa Suleyman** here:[https://lnkd.in/gQwfAbuc](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Flnkd%2Ein%2FgQwfAbuc&urlhash=fCIe&trk=public_post-text) Second, when it comes to Copilot, we are innovating rapidly, from chat to Cowork to Autopilots. We have also been super focused on improving the quality and performance of Copilot. Over the last three quarters, user satisfaction scores have doubled. And this quarter alone, we cut latency by 25 percent. Copilot usage intensity speaks for itself: · Number of conversations per user nearly doubled year over year · Average weekly engagement on par with Outlook and Teams · Number of customers with over 50K seats up 7X Y/Y · Customers deploying Copilot to majority of information workers, up nearly 75% QoQ And this quarter we will bring all our Copilot experiences together in one “super app” spanning both our consumer and commercial experiences. I’m greatly looking forward to this! A big Thank you to our employees and to our customers for continuing to put their trust in us. Read more here:[https://lnkd.in/gR3xdrUb](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Flnkd%2Ein%2FgR3xdrUb&urlhash=hWVO&trk=public_post-text)

[Eden Brownell](https://www.linkedin.com/in/edenbrownell?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 3mo


Not just going to be one of the AI hype minions in these comments. Perhaps the missing metric is the human cost of all that efficiency. Microsoft has announced layoffs equivalent to roughly 14% of its 2023 workforce over the past few years, even as it reports record revenue and AI growth. That is not the same as a 14% net reduction in headcount—but it is still a significant amount of disruption. The post talks about the importance of context and memory in AI systems. Organizations need context and memory too, and much of it lives in experienced employees and subject-matter experts. Are you measuring the expertise lost, the work that must be relearned, the trust damaged and the downstream quality effects of repeatedly removing people while celebrating record results? Models may be substitutable. Institutional knowledge often isn’t.

Impressive close,[Satya Nadella](https://www.linkedin.com/in/satyanadella?trk=public_post_comment-text) . The idea that every model should be substitutable is strategically important. But as Copilot moves from chat to Cowork and Autopilots, enterprises will need more than model portability—they will need decision continuity. Take a shipment-rerouting or payment-review workflow. If a model switch changes which cases are approved, escalated or delayed, the system may be technically resilient while the business becomes unpredictable. A practical next step for Foundry could be a decision-continuity test for every workflow: agreed policy boundaries, reference cases, acceptable outcome variance, shadow runs before switching, and automatic rollback when behaviour drifts. That would allow enterprises to optimize quality, latency and cost without rebuilding trust after every model change. The model can change. The enterprise promise should not.
